title: Lie-bracket controlled noncommuting Mirror composition
hypothesis: For unseen ordered pairs (A,B) and (B,A), a commutator-aware m composition lowers mean held-out pair loss by >=2% relative to native additive composition at matched bytes and by >=1% vs a byte-near ordinary ordered adapter, with at most 10% extra P95 latency.
physical_object: one shared task-update matrix basis or function block
mirror_coordinate: two cheap task codes m_A and m_B with an explicit order bit or Lie-bracket correction
logical_multiplicity: ordered composite behaviors from factor codes without a per-ordered-pair trained adapter
closest_controls: additive Task Arithmetic / native sequential gradient updates / full matrix products / MA-257

requirements.native: Train native additive task-vector composition and ordinary sequential A->B versus B->A updates. Include full small-matrix product, independent ordered-pair adapter as upper bound (not for hyperparameter search), and MA-257 factorized group-code comparison.
requirements.insertion: Before a shared block, decode two small task codes into structured operators and compose in order; optional single rank-corrected Lie bracket term is stored in a shared basis. Store the order bit, operator basis and any cached products.
requirements.method: Start with bounded noncommuting 2D/4D rotations/shears as a synthetic teacher, then learned tasks. Compute AB, BA and additive controls with identical active matmul count when possible; on fixed task-gradient fields estimate bracket via paired Hessian-vector products only from training support. Lock a heldout ordered-pair split; forbid fitting pair-specific m.
requirements.fixture: Four source primitive skills and six held-out ordered 2-skill combinations, each with disjoint support/dev/audit sequences; include commuting counterexamples where expected advantage is zero; d=32 shared two-layer MLP/attention.
requirements.hardware: Stage 1 CPU float64 algebra tests and float32 PyTorch training; stage 2 1 GPU for language-style tasks only after mechanism screen.

development.allowed: select code dimension, LR, stop condition only

resources.compute: training examples and updates, FLOPs or MACs, CPU/GPU P50/P95 with batch/dtype/hardware
resources.quality: Heldout pair CE, direction/order confusion rate, primitive-task retention, bytes incl ordering metadata, active multiplies and P95 CPU/GPU latency.

gates.PASS: Across five fresh seeds, median held-out ordered-pair CE improves by >=2% vs additive and >=1% vs best cheap ordered non-Mirror control, persistent bytes <= control, P95 <=1.10 control, and no held-out pair task training leaked.
gates.FAIL: Improvements vanish against native ordered product, any pair-specific trained model is secretly present, or commuting tasks show artificial order benefit indicating leakage.
gates.UNCERTAIN: Missing strong control, uncertain precision, insufficient heldout data, unmeasured runtime or CI overlap

alternative: Order effects may be too weak or native matrix multiplication already optimal; extra bracket correction may overfit and cost more than a simple ordered adapter.
uncertainty: HVP finite precision, optimizer step size, higher-order truncation, order-label correlation, task-seed variance; evaluate four step scales on dev and bootstrap by ordered pair.
stopping: Stop after 3 dev seeds then 5 fresh worlds; if cheap mechanism fails predeclared gate, record negative and do not tune fresh. Hardware unavailable => BLOCKED (not PASS).
prior_art_delta: Predict or correct order-dependent functional interaction using small Mirror commutator information, not mere Cartesian code combination already in MA-257.
limitations: An order bit does not create independent expert capacity; report unique target functions and the true number of independently trained primitive tasks.
